mil5.1.8:0.4: 8. Question on Cutting Off Unwholesome States
mil5.1.8:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, did the Tathāgata attain omniscience after burning up all unwholesome states, or did he attain omniscience while some unwholesome states remained?”
mil5.1.8:1.2: “Your majesty, the Blessed One attained omniscience after burning up all unwholesome states. No unwholesome state remained in the Blessed One.”
mil5.1.8:2.1: “But, venerable sir, did painful feeling ever arise in the Tathāgata’s body?”
mil5.1.8:2.2: “Yes, your majesty. At Rājagaha the Blessed One’s foot was pierced by a splinter, and an illness involving bloody discharge (dysentery) arose. When his body was congested, Jīvaka administered a purgative. When a wind ailment arose, the elder who was his attendant (Ānanda) sought out hot water.”
mil5.1.8:3.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, if the Tathāgata attained omniscience after burning up all unwholesome states, then the statement that the Blessed One’s foot was pierced by a splinter and that he suffered an illness with bloody discharge is false.
mil5.1.8:3.2: But if the Tathāgata’s foot were pierced by a splinter and he suffered an illness with bloody discharge, then the statement that the Tathāgata attained omniscience after burning up all unwholesome states is also false.
mil5.1.8:3.3: Venerable sir, there is no experiencing of feeling without kamma; all feeling is rooted in kamma, and one feels it by way of kamma alone. This double-horned dilemma has now come to you, and it must be resolved by you.”
mil5.1.8:4.1: “Certainly not, your majesty; not all feeling is rooted in kamma.
mil5.1.8:4.2: Feelings arise from eight causes, and by these causes many beings experience feeling.
mil5.1.8:4.4: Some feelings that arise here, your majesty, originate from wind;
mil5.1.8:4.7: some from the combination of the three; ...
mil5.1.8:4.8: some from the change of seasons; ...
mil5.1.8:4.9: some from careless or uneven conduct; ...
mil5.1.8:4.10: some from external assault or effort;
mil5.1.8:4.11: and some, your majesty, arise from the result of kamma.
mil5.1.8:4.12: By these eight causes many beings experience feeling.
mil5.1.8:4.13: Among these, those people who say ‘kamma afflicts beings’ are denying the other causes that exist for beings.
mil5.1.8:4.15: “Venerable Nāgasena, whatever is caused by wind, bile, phlegm, the combination of the three, the change of seasons, uneven conduct, or external assault: all of these originate from kamma alone. All of them come to be by way of kamma.”
mil5.1.8:5.1: “Your majesty, if all those ailments originated from kamma alone, they would not have distinct characteristics by category.
mil5.1.8:5.2: Wind, your majesty, is aggravated in ten ways: by cold, by heat, by hunger, by thirst, by overeating, by standing, by exertion, by violent motion, by assault, and by the result of kamma.
mil5.1.8:5.3: Of these, the nine kinds do not arise in the past or the future, but in the present existence. Therefore it should not be said that ‘all feeling originates from kamma.’
mil5.1.8:5.4: Bile, your majesty, is aggravated in three ways: by cold, by heat, and by unsuitable food.
mil5.1.8:5.5: Phlegm, your majesty, is aggravated in three ways: by cold, by heat, and by food and drink.
mil5.1.8:5.6: And the wind, the bile, and the phlegm, having been aggravated by their respective disturbances and having become mixed, bring on their own particular feeling.
mil5.1.8:5.7: Feeling born of the change of seasons arises through the change of seasons.
mil5.1.8:5.8: Feeling born of uneven conduct arises through uneven conduct.
mil5.1.8:5.9: As for feeling from external assault, your majesty, there is that which is mere action and there is that which is the result of kamma. Feeling born of the result of kamma arises through kamma done in the past.
mil5.1.8:5.10: Thus, your majesty, what is born of the result of kamma is small, and what remains is far greater.
mil5.1.8:5.11: In this matter fools overreach, saying, ‘It is all the result of kamma.’
mil5.1.8:5.12: That kamma cannot be determined without the knowledge of a Buddha.”
mil5.1.8:6.1: “As for the splinter that pierced the Blessed One’s foot, your majesty, that feeling was not born of wind, nor of bile, nor of phlegm, nor of their combination, nor of the change of seasons, nor of uneven conduct, nor of the result of kamma. It was from external assault alone.
